evals.prompt: Our Next.js repo ships on Vercel and we have no Algolia account. Provision Algolia for this Vercel project and get a working search. Give me the exact commands in order.
evals.expected_output: Vercel Marketplace provisioning: link the project, list existing resources, read live plans/metadata from --help, get approval, provision, then run the Algolia CLI through 'vercel env run' and validate a query with the search-only key.
expectations: Provisions through 'vercel integration add algolia' — does NOT use 'algolia auth signup' or 'algolia application create'
Runs 'vercel link' (with --project) before provisioning so the resource connects to the intended project
Checks for existing resources with 'vercel integration list' and/or 'vercel integration installations' BEFORE 'add'
Reads plans and metadata keys from 'vercel integration add algolia --help' instead of hardcoding a plan ID or region
Asks the user to approve the plan and the provider terms before running 'add'
Passes '--scope' and explicit '-e' environments on the 'add' command rather than relying on ambient scope and the all-three default
Runs the Algolia CLI through 'vercel env run -- ...' rather than pulling credentials to a file and hoping they are in the shell
Passes the SAME environment to 'vercel env run -e <env>' that it connected with '-e' on 'add' — does not leave it on its development default while connecting only production/preview
Bridges the injected names to the ones the Algolia CLI reads: exports ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID from ALGOLIA_APP_ID and ALGOLIA_API_KEY from the write or search key
Keeps the inner shell snippet single-quoted so the variables are expanded by the child process after 'env run' injects them, not by the outer shell beforehand
Guards the injected variables (for example '${ALGOLIA_APP_ID:?...}') so a missing value stops before the Algolia command runs, without claiming the guard proves the value came from Vercel
Does NOT 'source' or 'eval' an env file, and does not cat or print key values
Does not introduce a custom wrapper script, helper binary, or skill-directory path variable
Validates with 'algolia search' using the SEARCH key and reads nbHits rather than treating a clean exit as success
Hands search UI work to the instantsearch skill and offers 'npx skills add algolia/skills --skill instantsearch'

evals.prompt: Algolia might already be provisioned somewhere on this Vercel team, I'm not sure. Set it up for this project without risking a second Algolia application on our bill.
evals.expected_output: Inspect installations and resources first; if a resource exists, connect it to the project instead of provisioning a new one.
expectations: Runs 'vercel integration installations --integration algolia --format json' and 'vercel integration list --all --integration algolia --format=json' before anything that writes
States that 'vercel integration add' always creates a NEW resource even when the integration is already installed
If a resource already exists, uses 'vercel integration resource connect <resource> <project>' instead of 'add'
Does NOT provision 'a fresh one to be safe'
Shows the listed resources to the user and lets them choose when it is ambiguous which one is intended
If it mentions '--installation-id', attaches it to 'integration add' only — NOT to 'integration resource connect', which has no such flag
Does not claim that unrelated resources on the team make a deliberately new resource impossible
Describes the risk as a duplicate billed resource, and does not promise that a rerun cleanly yields a second working set of injected variables

evals.prompt: My Next.js app is on Vercel and Algolia was added from the Vercel Marketplace, but when I run the app locally process.env.ALGOLIA_APP_ID is undefined.
evals.expected_output: Verify the resource is connected, list the variable names, start the app through 'vercel env run', and map only browser-safe values to NEXT_PUBLIC_ in next.config.js.
expectations: Checks that the resource is connected to this project ('vercel integration list') and that the variables exist ('vercel env ls')
Starts the dev server through 'vercel env run -e <env> -- npm run dev' (or equivalent) rather than requiring a dotenv file
Checks that the environment being fetched matches the one the resource is connected to, and notes that 'vercel env run' defaults to development
Does NOT cat, diff, or line-print an env file, and does NOT create an un-ignored .bak copy of one

If it does pull a file, treats that as optional, names an explicit gitignored target, pulls the matching environment, and checks the existing file first rather than relying on the absence of '--yes' to prevent an overwrite

Adds a next.config.js 'env' block deriving NEXT_PUBLIC_ALGOLIA_APP_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_ALGOLIA_SEARCH_API_KEY from the raw ALGOLIA_ names Vercel injects, merging into any existing config and keeping wrappers rather than replacing it
Keeps ALGOLIA_WRITE_API_KEY server-side only, with no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix and no entry in the next.config.js 'env' block
This is a repair: does NOT import a demo index and does NOT start building search UI
Checks local overrides — a stale shell export or a local .env file takes precedence over the values 'vercel env run' fetches — before concluding the Vercel side is at fault
Notes that the browser-public variables are embedded at build time, so the local fix does not reach the deployed app until the next deployment

evals.prompt: Set up Algolia on Vercel for me. Heads up, I'm a member of three different Vercel teams and this repo isn't linked to a Vercel project yet.
evals.expected_output: Stop and ask which team and which project before provisioning; pin both explicitly on the commands.
expectations: Asks which of the three Vercel teams should own and be billed for the resource — does not pick one
Asks which project to link, and runs 'vercel link --project <name>' before provisioning
Passes '--scope' (or '--team') explicitly rather than relying on the ambient active scope
Does not run 'vercel integration add' before the team and project are confirmed
Notes that 'vercel integration add' runs non-interactively when an agent is detected, so no prompt will appear to catch a wrong scope
Does not invent extra approval gates beyond the open scope, plan, terms and environment decisions

evals.prompt: We self-host our Rails app on our own AWS EC2 boxes. We need Algolia from scratch — no account, no app ID, nothing.
evals.expected_output: Not this skill. There is no Vercel in the picture, so account and application provisioning belongs to algolia-quickstart.
expectations: Does NOT route to Vercel Marketplace provisioning
Routes account and application creation to algolia-quickstart ('algolia auth signup', 'algolia application create')
Does not suggest adopting Vercel to obtain Algolia

evals.prompt: I have a Next.js app. Add a search results page with faceted filtering using Algolia. I already have my app ID, search-only key and my 'products' index.
evals.expected_output: Not this skill. Next.js alone does not imply Vercel, and credentials plus index already exist — this is UI work.
expectations: Does NOT route to algolia-vercel — Next.js alone is not evidence of Vercel hosting
Does NOT propose provisioning anything; credentials and an index already exist
Routes to instantsearch (or the implementation-planning suite) for the search results page and facets

evals.prompt: Our Next.js app is deployed on Vercel. We've had a standalone Algolia account for two years with our 'products' index and our own API keys in our secret manager. Add autocomplete to the header.
evals.expected_output: The existing standalone application stays standalone. Vercel hosting alone is not a reason to provision a duplicate; this is UI work.
expectations: Keeps the existing standalone Algolia application — does NOT provision a Vercel Marketplace resource
Does NOT run 'vercel integration add algolia' just because the app is hosted on Vercel
Uses the credentials already in the user's secret manager
Routes the autocomplete implementation to instantsearch
If it raises the Marketplace option at all, frames it as an explicit user choice to migrate, not a step in this task

evals.prompt: I just got a fresh empty Algolia application from the Vercel Marketplace. Load some example data and prove search actually works before we build any UI.
evals.expected_output: Additive ndjson import into a new index with the write key, then a search with the search-only key, both run through 'vercel env run'.
expectations: Writes ndjson (one JSON object per line, not a JSON array) with an objectID on each record
Imports into a new, clearly-example index name
Does NOT run 'algolia indices clear' or 'algolia indices delete' to prepare
Passes '-w' to the import so the validation query does not race indexing
Supplies credentials as ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID / ALGOLIA_API_KEY exported inside a 'vercel env run' child process, rather than 'algolia auth login' or the deprecated 'algolia profile add'
Does not reach for a bundled helper script or a path to the installed skill directory
Uses the WRITE key for the import and the SEARCH key for the validation query
Reports the actual nbHits and a matched record instead of asserting success
Reports what the CLI query returned rather than claiming end-to-end or deployed search is working

evals.prompt: Checked with 'vercel integration list' and our Algolia resource 'storefront-search' is already there and already connected to the 'storefront' project. The local env still has nothing. Take it from here.
evals.expected_output: Nothing to provision and nothing to connect. Confirm the variable names, run the Algolia CLI through 'vercel env run', and validate read-only.
expectations: Runs NEITHER 'vercel integration add' NOR 'vercel integration resource connect' — the intended resource is already connected
Goes straight to 'vercel env ls' and 'vercel env run -e <the connected environment>'
Treats the missing local variables as a credentials/environment problem, not as evidence that provisioning failed
Inspects variable names without printing values
Does not seed an example index or build UI for this repair — validates against an index that already exists, and only offers seeding if there is no data to search

If a variable is still missing or points at the wrong application, considers the wrong fetched environment, a resource connected to another project, a '--prefix'ed variable name, or a stale local shell/.env value overriding the fetched one — before re-provisioning

evals.prompt: We're on Vercel with no Algolia yet. Set Algolia up and put a working search box on our products page.
evals.expected_output: Provision, wire credentials, validate — then keep going and actually build the search UI with instantsearch rather than ending the turn at the query.
expectations: Does NOT end the turn at 'search returns hits, now use the instantsearch skill' — the user asked for a search box
Loads instantsearch (offering 'npx skills add algolia/skills --skill instantsearch' if it is not available) and continues into the UI work
Passes the index name, the record shape, and the credential VARIABLE names to the UI step — not raw key values
Tells the user to start the dev server through 'vercel env run' so the injected variables reach the next.config.js mapping
Does not treat a minimal InstantSearch component as inherently wrong; writes it from the instantsearch guidance and the installed package version
Tells the user that the deployed app needs a redeploy before the browser-public variables change

evals.prompt: I ran the search validation command against my new index and it failed. Tell me what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Ask what the response actually said, then branch — an index-not-found error, a zero-hit result, and an API-key error have different causes.
expectations: Distinguishes an index-not-found error (missing or misnamed index) from a successful response with nbHits = 0
Does NOT claim that a missing or nonexistent index returns zero hits

Treats a search-key failure conditionally — key ACLs, per-index restrictions, credentials from two different applications, or a variable that was never injected — rather than asserting it was never injected
Asks for or inspects the actual error text before prescribing a fix
Does NOT propose deleting the project's environment variables as a default remedy

evals.prompt: We already had a DATABASE_URL clash so our Algolia resource was connected with --prefix. 'vercel env ls' shows ALGOLIA2_ALGOLIA_APP_ID, ALGOLIA2_ALGOLIA_SEARCH_API_KEY and ALGOLIA2_ALGOLIA_WRITE_API_KEY. Get a validation query running.
evals.expected_output: Use the prefixed names exactly as 'vercel env ls' reports them, consistently in the env run block and in the next.config.js mapping.
expectations: Uses the exact prefixed names the user reported rather than the unprefixed defaults
Does NOT invent a different transformation of the names (for example dropping the second ALGOLIA_ segment) — it takes them from 'vercel env ls' as-is
Still exports ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID and ALGOLIA_API_KEY for the Algolia CLI, sourced from the prefixed variables
Applies the same prefixed names in the next.config.js NEXT_PUBLIC_ mapping if it touches that
Does NOT re-provision or reconnect the resource to get unprefixed names

evals.prompt: Confusing one. 'vercel env ls' shows ALGOLIA_APP_ID on this project and it's the new application. But my .env.local and an exported ALGOLIA_APP_ID in my shell both still point at our old Algolia app, and commands keep hitting the old one even under 'vercel env run'. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Local values win. 'vercel env run' layers fetched records first, then local .env files, then the process environment — so the shell export and .env.local override what Vercel fetched.
expectations: Identifies the local shell export and .env.local as the cause — they take precedence over the values 'vercel env run' fetches
States the layering correctly: fetched Vercel records are lowest, then local .env files, then the shell/process environment, with the last one winning
Does NOT claim that 'vercel env run' always overrides local values, or that a name appearing in 'vercel env ls' proves the command used that value
Notes that a '${VAR:?...}' guard cannot catch this, because the variable is set — just set to the wrong value
Inspects the conflicting names in BOTH the shell and the local .env file without printing key values
Resolves only the stale entries (unset the export, correct or remove the .env.local line) rather than deleting the project's Vercel environment variables
Does NOT re-provision or reconnect the resource to fix it
